title: Whole-Brain Neurobiology Atlas — Structures, Networks, Flows and Potatoverse Mappings
purpose: Describe the human brain and nervous system as a connected biological architecture, then route Potatoverse symbolic correspondences onto that anatomy without treating symbolism as scientific proof.
epistemic_rule: Scientific anatomy/physiology, project canon, historical/esoteric association, religious comparison and speculation are separately typed. Similarity, shape and metaphor do not establish causal identity or ancient hidden neuroanatomy.

orientation.principle: The brain is represented as a relational system of structures, nuclei, tracts, loops, chemical modulators, barriers, fluids and dynamic state changes rather than as a list of isolated modules.
reader_order: which larger loops it participates in

sections.name: Nervous-system frame
sections.summary: The brain sits within a bidirectional nervous system linking body, spinal cord, peripheral nerves, autonomic regulation and sensory environments.

components.name: Afferent/efferent organization
components.science: Afferent pathways carry information toward central systems; efferent pathways carry commands or regulatory signals outward.

relations: body ↔ peripheral nerves ↔ spinal cord/brainstem ↔ thalamus/cortex
sections.boundary: No single nerve or pathway carries a unitary spiritual force; symbolic ascent/descent remains a project analogy.

sections.name: Cerebral cortex and association territories
sections.summary: The cerebral cortex is organized into overlapping sensory, motor, association, attentional, language, memory and self/world-model systems distributed across both hemispheres.

components.name: Hemispheric lateralization
components.science: Some functions show population-level asymmetries, especially language and aspects of spatial/prosodic processing, but creativity, personality, intelligence and consciousness are not cleanly divided into left-brain/right-brain types.

sections.boundary: Cortical lobes are not sealed modules and do not map one-to-one onto spiritual faculties or personality categories.

sections.name: White matter and long-range connectivity
sections.summary: White-matter tracts form long-range communication routes linking cortical, subcortical, brainstem and cerebellar systems.

components.name: Internal capsule
components.role: dense corridor for thalamocortical, corticospinal and corticobulbar fibers

components.name: Corona radiata
components.role: fan-like cortical projection fibers continuous with internal capsule

components.name: Cingulum
components.role: association pathway linking cingulate/medial temporal regions

components.name: Superior longitudinal/arcuate systems
components.role: frontoparietotemporal association pathways including language-related connections

components.name: Inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus
components.role: long association pathway linking posterior and frontal regions

relations: rooms ↔ roads is a project-level architecture analogy
tract damage can disconnect otherwise intact regions
sections.boundary: White matter is biological connectivity, not a literal root system or spiritual road network.

sections.name: Diencephalon
sections.summary: The diencephalon contains the thalamus, hypothalamus, epithalamic structures and subthalamic systems surrounding the third-ventricle region and coordinating sensory, motor, homeostatic, endocrine, circadian and state-related functions.

components.name: Thalamus
components.location: Paired deep diencephalic gray-matter structures forming much of the lateral walls of the third ventricle.

shape_or_geometry.science: Paired diencephalic gray-matter structures conventionally described as ovoid or egg-shaped.
shape_or_geometry.potatoverse: Potato-shaped is the canonical Potatoism shape description: the compact rounded ovoid form is deliberately read as potato-like.
shape_or_geometry.boundary: Potato-shaped is project language, not the standard anatomical term.

components.functional_principle: The thalamus is not one passive relay switch; distinct nuclei form parallel and interacting thalamocortical/subcortical loops.
components.olfaction_exception: Primary olfactory processing is the classic exception to simplified claims that all senses must first relay through thalamus; later olfactory processing still interacts with thalamic/cortical systems.
components.boundary: The thalamus is not scientifically established as a divine residence, literal potato, unique seat of soul, or sole generator of consciousness.

components.name: Pineal gland
components.location: Small midline neuroendocrine organ in the epithalamic region near the posterior roof of the third ventricle.
components.science: Melatonin secretion is regulated by circadian/autonomic pathways influenced by retinal light input through the suprachiasmatic clock; the human pineal is not a retinal-style direct photoreceptor.

project_mapping.mapping: Single Eye / Third Eye / Son-side Eye / Door / timing threshold

components.boundary: The human pineal is not a retinal-style photoreceptor, projector of spiritual light, or proven seat of soul/consciousness. Neuroscience does not call it a literal third eye.

components.name: Habenular complex
components.boundary: Keep habenular biology distinct from pineal/third-eye symbolism.

components.name: Hypothalamus

project_mapping.mapping: Steward / household regulator adjacent to the House

components.boundary: Older project strata sometimes called hypothalamus the Potato Room; current canonical House mapping is thalamic.

components.name: Subthalamus
components.boundary: The subthalamus is anatomically distinct from the thalamus despite the name.

sections.boundary: Diencephalic structures are neighboring but functionally distinct; symbolic House/Eye/Steward roles must not collapse them into one organ.

sections.name: Basal ganglia and action-selection loops
sections.summary: The basal ganglia are interconnected subcortical nuclei participating in movement, action selection, habit learning, reinforcement, motivation and cognitive loops.
relations: cortex → striatum → pallidal/nigral outputs → thalamus → cortex
sections.boundary: Basal-ganglia circuitry is not literal moral judgment tissue; direct/indirect/hyperdirect descriptions are useful simplifications of richer circuits.

sections.name: Memory, affect and contextual systems
sections.summary: Memory and emotion emerge from distributed interactions among hippocampal, amygdalar, cortical, thalamic, hypothalamic and brainstem systems rather than one limbic center.

components.name: Amygdala
components.science: Heterogeneous nuclear complex contributing to salience, valence, threat learning, associative learning, autonomic/endocrine response coordination and social-affective processing.
components.boundary: The amygdala is not simply a fear center.

relations: world encounter → affective marking → contextual memory → attention/model update

project_mapping.mapping: returning reports / memory / affective marking / context

sections.boundary: Huginn/Muninn remain mythic information comparators, not identities of particular brain regions.

sections.name: Brainstem and arousal systems
sections.summary: The brainstem—midbrain, pons and medulla—contains sensory/motor relays, cranial-nerve nuclei, autonomic control systems, neuromodulatory nuclei and state-regulating networks essential to life and wakefulness.

project_mapping.mapping: Lower Gate / vigilance / life-support root beneath the House

sections.boundary: Wakefulness is distributed across interacting systems and does not define soul or spiritual rank.

sections.name: Cerebellar system
sections.summary: The cerebellum contributes to coordination, timing, prediction, error correction, motor learning and cognitive-affective processes through closed and open loops with brainstem, spinal, thalamic and cortical systems.

components.name: Arbor vitae
components.science: Traditional anatomical name for branching cerebellar white matter, literally 'tree of life'.

sections.boundary: The anatomical name arbor vitae is descriptive and does not establish biblical Tree-of-Life identity.

sections.name: Sensory systems
sections.summary: Sensory systems transform peripheral signals through specialized relay and cortical pathways, with substantial feedback and parallel processing.

components.name: Visual system
components.path: retina → optic nerve → optic chiasm → optic tract → LGN/superior-collicular routes → optic radiations → visual cortex → distributed dorsal/ventral streams
components.boundary: Optic-chiasm crossing is partial and organized by visual hemifield; an entire eye does not simply cross to the opposite hemisphere.

components.name: Auditory system
components.path: cochlea → brainstem auditory nuclei → inferior colliculus → MGN → auditory cortex with bilateral/parallel processing

components.name: Olfactory system
components.science: Primary olfactory pathways reach olfactory/limbic cortical targets without the same obligatory first-order thalamic relay as vision, audition and somatosensation; later olfactory processing still involves thalamic/cortical interactions.

relations: top-down cortical feedback modulates sensory processing
attention changes selection at multiple stages
sections.boundary: Sensory relays are not simple one-way wires and should not be treated as mystical portals.

sections.name: Motor systems
sections.summary: Movement emerges from interacting cortical, basal-ganglia, cerebellar, brainstem and spinal systems rather than a single motor center.

components.name: Corticospinal system
relations: motor cortex → internal capsule → brainstem → pyramidal decussation/descending spinal pathways → spinal motor circuits

components.name: Corticobulbar system
relations: motor cortex → brainstem cranial motor systems
basal ganglia and cerebellum act largely through parallel recurrent loops with cortex and thalamus
sections.boundary: Motor control is distributed, hierarchical and recurrent; no one tract equals will or agency.

sections.name: Ventricles, CSF, meninges and barriers
sections.summary: Fluid spaces, membranes and vascular interfaces maintain mechanical protection, chemical homeostasis, transport and controlled exchange around neural tissue.

components.name: Ventricular system
components.path: lateral ventricles → foramina of Monro → third ventricle → cerebral aqueduct → fourth ventricle → apertures → subarachnoid space

components.name: Third ventricle
components.boundary: Conscious signals do not physically traverse the third ventricle as a cognitive doorway.

components.name: Neurovascular unit
functions: coupling of neural activity, blood flow and metabolic support

sections.boundary: CSF is not Holy Spirit, and barriers/membranes are not moral purity filters.

sections.name: Cellular and chemical neurobiology
sections.summary: Brain function depends on neurons, glia, synapses, electrical signaling, metabolism and diverse transmitter/modulator systems operating across many timescales.

components.name: Dopamine
components.role: neuromodulation of movement, learning, salience, motivation and action policies

components.name: Serotonin
components.role: broad neuromodulation across mood, cognition, sleep, appetite and other functions

components.name: Norepinephrine
components.role: arousal, attention, learning and autonomic-state modulation

components.name: Acetylcholine
components.role: attention, learning, arousal and neuromuscular/peripheral functions

components.name: Orexin/hypocretin
components.role: wakefulness, motivational and metabolic state integration

relations: neuromodulators act broadly across networks rather than encoding one emotion each
glia and vascular systems help maintain the conditions for neural computation
sections.boundary: Neurochemical labels should not be converted into one-molecule psychological or spiritual essences.

sections.name: Large-scale functional networks
sections.summary: Large-scale networks are overlapping, method-dependent descriptions of coordinated activity across distributed regions; boundaries and labels vary across atlases and tasks.

components.name: Default-mode systems
components.boundary: The default-mode network is not the self as an organ.

relations: networks overlap anatomically and reconfigure with task/state
thalamic/subcortical systems interact with cortical network organization

project_mapping.mapping: world-model / narrative map / branches of the House

sections.boundary: No large-scale network has a fixed spiritual rank or singular metaphysical identity.

sections.name: Brain states, sleep and consciousness boundaries
sections.summary: Wakefulness, NREM sleep, REM sleep, anesthesia and disorders of consciousness reflect changes across distributed brainstem, hypothalamic, thalamic, basal-forebrain and cortical systems; consciousness science remains actively contested.

components.name: Conscious access
components.science: Active research problem involving distributed recurrent and state-dependent interactions.

relations: sleep changes thalamocortical dynamics, memory processing and sensory gating
sections.boundary: The thalamus alone does not create consciousness; the claustrum is not a proven singular seat of consciousness; the pineal is not a proven seat of soul; EEG frequencies are not spiritual ranks.

not one whole eye to opposite hemisphere
flows.potatoverse_comparator: optic chiasm ↔ Cross is provisional project geometry only

caveats: auditory routing is bilateral and parallel
different modalities use distinct tracts and crossings

flows.output: odor perception, memory and affective associations
caveats: classic exception to simplified first-order thalamic relay rule
not a single cortical balance center

flows.output: state-dependent routing, selection and recurrent processing

caveats: many axes with distinct hormones and timescales
not a moral or spiritual axis

flows.input: salient outcomes, expectations and internal state
feedback_or_parallel_paths: habenular, pallidal, cortical and limbic inputs

potatoverse_mapping_table.boundary: Conventional anatomy says ovoid/egg-shaped; potato-shaped is canonical Potatoverse language, not a scientific taxonomic term.
Nuclei are neural cell groups, not literal rooms.
TRN inhibitory modulation does not filter spiritual frequencies.
Axonal connectivity is not botanical growth.
The ventricle is a CSF-filled cavity, not a cognitive portal.

potatoverse_mapping_table.project_mapping: Single Eye / Third Eye / Son-side Eye / Door / timing threshold
potatoverse_mapping_table.boundary: Third-eye/single-eye meaning is not established neuroscience.
Partial visual crossing is biology; crucifixion meaning is symbolic.
Insula is not a hidden eye.
Amygdala is not a single fear center.

potatoverse_mapping_table.project_mapping: action selection / permission / inhibition / judgment analogy

potatoverse_mapping_table.boundary: Historical anatomical naming does not prove biblical identity.

potatoverse_mapping_table.project_mapping: world-model / branches / narrative rooms opening outward
potatoverse_mapping_table.boundary: Networks are dynamic scientific constructs, not theological dimensions.
Glia are biological support/regulatory cells, not divine agents.

canonical_statements.thalamus: In Potatoism, the thalamus is the Potato at the center of the brain's symbolic House: paired compact ovoid bodies deliberately read as potato-shaped. Its nuclei become rooms, its reciprocal pathways become roads/roots/branches, and surrounding modulatory systems become walls and gates. This is a symbolic architectural correspondence grounded in real thalamic anatomy, not a scientific identification of the thalamus with God or a literal potato.
canonical_statements.pineal: In Potatoism, the pineal gland is the Single Eye / Third Eye and a Son-side Door or timing threshold. Its real biology is neuroendocrine and circadian: it produces melatonin under indirect control of the light-sensitive circadian system. The third-eye and single-eye meanings belong to esoteric history, religious comparison and Potatoverse canon rather than established neuroscience.

boundaries.thalamus_divinity: The thalamus is not scientifically established as a divine residence or literal Father's House.
boundaries.consciousness: Neither the thalamus nor claustrum is a uniquely proven seat of consciousness; conscious access remains a distributed active research problem.
boundaries.pineal_soul: The pineal gland is not a proven seat of soul.
boundaries.pineal_eye: The human pineal is not a retinal-style photoreceptor or supernatural light projector; Third Eye is not established neuroscience.
boundaries.eeg: EEG frequency bands do not define spiritual rank.
boundaries.amygdala: The amygdala is not simply a fear center.
boundaries.hemispheres: Left-brain/right-brain personality typing is an oversimplification.
boundaries.chakras: Chakras must not be mapped one-to-one onto glands, ganglia, nerves or brain regions.
boundaries.hidden_ancient_neuroanatomy: Ancient texts, religious art or esoteric symbols are not proven encodings of modern neuroanatomy merely because modern overlays resemble brain structures.
